newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-AUSTRALIAN-BORN BROTHERS HAILED BY ENGLISH CROWDS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIAN-BORN BROTHERS HAILED BY ENGLISH CROWDS.

text.p: Brothers with distinctive Australian accents, bristling with undiluted antipodean aggression, were cheered to the echo at London's two cricket cathedrals at the weekend.
Overdue sunshine had not softened the brains of capacity crowds at The Oval and Lord's.

Instead, they were celebrating the achievements of Adam and Ben Hollioake, born in Melbourne, raised in England and instrumental in giving the national cricket team a 3-0 one-day series victory over Australia.
The new England selection committee had been expected to pick 25-year-old Surrey captain Adam for the one-day series.
In a bold move unprecedented in recent years, the selectors went one better, picking 19-year-old Ben as well after just five first class matches.
Adam was an immediate success after a tentative start at Headingley last Thursday, scoring an unbeaten 66, finishing the match with a six and winning the man-of-the-match award.
On Saturday, Adam ended the match at The Oval with a brace of fours while scoring 53 not out.
The following day it was Ben's turn in the sun.
Watched by his parents, John and Daria, Ben celebrated his first visit to the game's world headquarters with an astonishing innings of 63 from the pivotal number three spot.
Astonishing not only for the runs but also for the style.
Hollioake tore into the unofficial world champions' likely test attack, striking 11 fours and a six from 48 balls.
"I was a bit surprised to be playing today but it was quite a good day to step inside Lord's for the first time," Hollioake said.
"It was brilliant, I loved it. I was not as nervous as I thought I would be, though still a bit nervous.
"In the end, I was annoyed at getting out because I thought I had a chance of going on for three figures."
The brothers were both born in Melbourne, moving to England in 1985 where they lived for eight years before their father's job as an off-shore engineer brought him back to Perth.
Adam stayed with Surrey while Ben returned to join his parents for a year before also taking up a contract with the south London club.

They are the first brothers to represent England since Peter and Dick Richardson in 1957 while Ben is the youngest England player since Brian Close was called up at the age of 18 against the 1949 New Zealanders.
Off the field, apparently, they are equally competitive.
"Everybody knows there's rivalry between me and Adam but it's all good fun," Ben commented on Sunday.
"When I got back to the dressing room, he said: 'Well done, but I still think you're too skinny'."
Can they make the grade in test cricket?
England captain Mike Atherton had no doubts when asked about Adam at his post-match news conference on Saturday.
"Definitely," Atherton replied.
But, as Atherton separately acknowledged, one-day cricket bears little relation to the five-day game. "When the test matches come, it will be a very different scenario," he warned.
At the moment, the English cricketing public couldn't care less. The sun is shining, the team is winning and the Hollioake brothers are the toast of the nation.
